title: Spectral Geometry of Attention: From Information Routing to Uncertainty
claim: Measuring a mechanism under the right geometry removes a hidden bias, and that diagnostic can be turned into a practical uncertainty signal.
layout: 3 framed blocks, left-to-right; blue vs red boxes contrast geometries
description: The figure has three bordered blocks read left to right. The left block zooms from an LLM diagram into a transformer block and then a multi-head attention module. It ends with the map A: L²(μ) → L²(π). Below that are two framed surface sketches. A blue frame is labeled Euclidean scenario, and a red frame is labeled Probability geometry scenario. In the red frame the μ surface is warped. The center block is titled Sink bias parametrization. It has a line plot of sink score and two metrics against α. Under the plot are three attention-map heatmaps (routing, sink-biased, sink) and, under those, three spectra plots. The right block has yellow attention maps labeled Certain and Uncertain, with blue zoom insets. A red box and arrow mark the routing failure.
caption: Teaser: (Left block) Our work studies transformers' attention as a functional map between Hilbert spaces equipped with an inner product. The properties of the operator change with the standard Euclidean measure (Blue) and with an intrinsic probability geometry measure (Red). (Center Block) Parametrizing row stochastic causal map interpolating ($\alpha$) between a copy map and a sink map, we show that the Euclidean spectrum of the matrix is biased towards the sink, while reweighting the input measure relaxes this bias. (Right Block) We leverage our insights to design an uncertainty quantifier, identifying uncertainty as a routing capability collapse in certain selected heads (red box in the uncertain model).
abstract: In this work, we study transformer attention through the lens of spectral geometry and operator theory. We view each attention head as a functional map between Hilbert spaces of functions on the token sequence and derive a Token Difference Operator, whose spectral structure controls how token-space information is routed to the output. We show that standard Euclidean spectra are structurally biased by sinks, conflating mass concentration with genuine routing capacity. By recasting token space in the intrinsic probability geometry induced by attention, the token difference spectrum disentangles sink effects from routing capacity and provides a spectral description of the dimensionality of the head output. This yields a unified framework for analyzing attention maps, explaining sinks, routing collapse, and output dimensionality within a single operator-theoretic framework. In practice, by grounding attention heuristics in spectral geometry, we develop a novel attention-based uncertainty estimator that complements probability-based scores, with the largest gains on long-context inputs.
